Deep admiration for the perseverance of Sviatlana @Tsihanouskaya. For years, she has been standing up for democracy in Belarus, at great risk to her own life. So it was an honour to receive her today.

We discussed the importance of a democratic and stable Belarus for the security of all of Europe. The Netherlands will continue to actively support the protection of human rights and the release of all political prisoners.

Don’t be naive, pursue a pragmatic approach that takes account of our own interests, and reach out to the rest of the world: just a few elements I touched on in my speech this morning on international security at the Next Gen Security Conference.  

Today and tomorrow experts are meeting at the Peace Palace in The Hague to discuss a question that the Netherlands, and Europe as a whole, need to address: what will make us strong and keep us safe? 

I believe the answer to that question lies in three principles at the heart of Dutch foreign and security policy. First, we must remain fully committed to the rule of law and the international legal order. 

In addition, the transatlantic alliance remains crucial for our security, and that means Europe will have to do more to make NATO stronger. Finally, the Netherlands and Europe must forge new partnerships and renew existing ones. 

Curious about my full answer to this question? Read my speech via https://t.co/gj1DJD4c4r

The Netherlands and Moldova work together closely in a variety of areas. Today I welcomed @sandumaiamd to the Netherlands to discuss and strengthen our ties.

Since the start of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine, Moldova has been a key partner for neighbouring Ukraine and the rest of Europe. The Netherlands continues to support Moldova in this regard and therefore backs Moldova’s accession to the EU. 

Today, we pledged €1.5 million in additional support for Moldova, with a focus on defence cooperation and strengthening Moldova’s cybersecurity and hybrid resilience.

Our strong ties offer opportunities for further growth, for example through collaboration in the areas of horticulture and sustainable energy. I look forward to working on this with President Sandu.

South Africa is one of our most important partners in Africa, particularly where trade is concerned. We work together in fields such as climate action, cybersecurity and green hydrogen, and we are closely aligned on issues like human rights and gender equality. 

So with that in mind it was good to get acquainted with President Cyril Ramaphosa of South Africa today. We discussed the importance of working together, both at bilateral level and in multilateral forums such as the G20 and the United Nations. We also talked about geopolitical issues, including the wars in the Middle East, Ukraine and Sudan.

If there’s one thing the Netherlands excels at, it is dealing with water. India has shown considerable interest in our expertise in the field of water management. We’re looking to deepen our cooperation in this area. 

That’s why, together with Prime Minister @narendramodi, I visited an icon among Dutch water engineering structures: the Afsluitdijk barrier dam.

Here, we learned about the history of the dam, how it protects us from flooding and how it enables innovative and sustainable forms of energy.
 
🇳🇱🤝🇮🇳

At times of international uncertainty, it’s especially important that we can rely on like-minded and valued partners. Both India and the Netherlands attach great importance to democracy, good governance and a world order based on rules and justice.
 
My discussion with Prime Minister @narendramodi this evening included the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which has resulted in high energy prices. As in the Netherlands, the impact on India has been severe too. So it’s vital that this conflict bebrought to an end and that a lasting solution be found. We also spoke about the case regarding the abduction of Insiya to India by her father.

The friendship between India and the Netherlands is in full bloom, asunderscored by the visit of Prime Minister @narendramodi to the Netherlands. We’re now taking that bond to an even higher level as we enter into a Strategic Partnership with one another.

This partnership is already bearing fruit. Multiple letters of intent have been or are being signed this weekend in such areas as defence cooperation, the development of major new technologies and innovations, healthcare and water management. ASML and Tata Electronics have also signed a letter of intent in a key step towards deeper cooperation in the semiconductor industry. 

This builds on the major, historic trade agreement concluded between India and the EU earlier this year. In short, we’re making tremendous strides in our cooperation, creating a true win-win situation.

Masha danki and hopefully see you soon! My visit to Dushi Korsou was one I won’t forget in a hurry. 

At the Parera naval base, the Commander briefed me on the impact of geopolitical tensions on the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. He also spoke about the important work carried out by the coastguard and the Royal Netherlands Marechaussee in combating drug trafficking and providing assistance during disasters, such as hurricanes. 

This was followed by a wonderful and, above all, impressive visit to the Tula Museum. Tula was the leader of the largest slave revolt on Curaçao. It is incredibly important that we continue to face up to that dark period in our shared history, honour the heroes of that time and learn from it for our shared future. The Tula Museum brings that story to life and celebrates the proud culture of the island and the region. 

After an informative meeting on community building in Bandabou, we continued the programme with a visit to the Aqualectra Battery Storage Park. This is a key step towards achieving more sustainable energy consumption on the island.   
 
Of course, a visit to the Blue Wave Fanshop was a must. It’s quite special that two countries of the Kingdom are taking part in the World Cup. It will be Curaçao’s first time, and we all hope they beat Germany in the group stage ;) 

Many thanks to everyone on the islands who made this wonderful, productive and educational trip possible!

Curaçao is flourishing and growing. Upon arrival, I was warmly welcomed by Prime Minister Gilmar Pisas to my last destination of this visit: beautiful Curaçao!

During talks with Prime Minister Pisas, the president of Curaçao’s parliament, members of parliament and the cabinet, a number of current issues were discussed. One example was geopolitical tensions around the world  – including in this region – and their impact on the cost of living.
Another important topic we discussed was administrative cooperation between our countries. 

With this in mind, we looked ahead to the plans to organise a Kingdom-wide conference – a recurring meeting between the four governments as equal partners within the Kingdom. This would allow relevant developments within the Kingdom to be discussed, as well as ways our countries could work together more closely and make full use of opportunities to improve people’s lives.

Felis dia! Aruba is buzzing with energy. The day got off to a great start with a wonderful visit to Arikok National Park. In this vast nature reserve, I learnt about Aruba’s efforts in the areas of sustainability, biodiversity and nature restoration.

During a sports day, I saw young sporting talent in action. A wonderful event that highlights the importance of sport and exercise for young people and how talent development is encouraged here on the island. It also makes young people here aware of the importance of a healthy lifestyle. 

I spoke with the Speaker of Parliament and various party leaders about good (financial) governance, the island’s socio-economic development and effective cooperation within the Kingdom. 

Finally, I visited Reina Beatrix Airport. Here I saw how hard work is being done to modernise the airport; this is important for tourism and the 
economy. Aruba’s role as a regional tourism hub is being further strengthened. 

Aruba recently celebrated the island’s special status. Much has been achieved since then. This visit gives me great confidence in the future of this beautiful island.

Many thanks to my colleague Mike Eman for an especially hospitable welcome in Aruba. 

The prime minister and I discussed the consequences of the geopolitical situation concerning Venezuela. Aruba is heavily dependent on imports and is therefore directly affected by high global prices. Plans to diversify the economy and improve the social situation of Arubans are therefore very important. Education, housing, good healthcare and sustainability are high on the agenda in this regard.

Together with Aruba’s cabinet, we looked ahead to our countries’ cooperation in the coming years. By sharing knowledge and expertise within the Kingdom, we can achieve a great deal.

Masha, thank you, Bonaire 🇧🇶 A fruitful working visit focused on creating a sustainable, economically strong and liveable island for everyone.

In recent years, the Netherlands has worked together with Bonaire to improve people’s livelihoods. As well as a higher minimum wage, affordable housing is also of great importance. More than 250 social housing units are currently being completed. A wonderful project where people can find a home. 

A much-discussed issue is Selibon Lagun. Due to unsafe storage practices, this landfill site has for some time posed serious risks to the environment and the local community. I went to see for myself how this problem can be resolved. It is important that the improvements already underway are now seen through to completion, with the health of Bonaire’s residents as the top priority. 

Many thanks to Governor John Soliano, Acting Representative of the State Jan Helmond, the Island Council and the Executive Council, and all the residents for the warm welcome. Today I have seen that Bonaire is an island with great potential. For example, in the areas of infrastructure and good, affordable housing, but also in relation to nature, the environment and climate issues. 

The Netherlands wants to help seize the opportunities that lie ahead. That is a joint task. Nos ta un Reino!

The beautiful island of Sint Eustatius is a place with a rich history. You can see and feel this when you visit Fort Oranje and the Heritage Centre. Here, the history of ‘Statia’ comes to life. There is now, rightly so, a greater focus on the heroes who fought for freedom from slavery. It’s crucial that we continue to pay attention to this horrific period of our shared history.

I also visited the GTI oil terminal, which provides around 200 jobs on the island. The terminal is a crucial link in the energy supply chain in the Caribbean region. This is particularly important in times of geopolitical unrest. 

I spoke with the Governor, the Executive Council and members of the Island Council about how we can further strengthen local government. So that together we can give the island an economic and social boost. Safety, good education and accessible healthcare play an important role in this. 

The island’s most important public holiday, ‘Statia Day’, will be extra special this year. November marks the 250th anniversary of Sint Eustatius becoming the first state in the world to recognise the US as an independent nation with ‘The First Salute’. The team updated me on the preparations for all the festivities.

Many thanks to Governor Francis for the warm welcome and the wonderful visit to Sint Eustatius.

After arriving on St Eustatius it was good to meet Governor Alida Francis, the Kingdom’s first woman governor and a born-and-bred Statian. In short, someone uniquely qualified to tell me about how things are going on the island.
 
Together with the other members of the executive council we discussed the island’s working relationship with The Hague, safety and security on St Eustatius, and the challenges facing the island in areas like infrastructure, climate action and waste management.
 
It was a great start to my visit to this small but beautiful island.

A wonderful visit to Saba today. The island is also known as ‘the unspoilt Queen’. And rightly so, for its natural beauty is unparalleled. As is the determination to preserve it for future generations. 

It’s good to see how much work is being done on Saba. The construction of the new, hurricane-proof seaport (Black Rocks Harbour) is particularly striking. 

During my visit to the Saba Enrichment Centre in St. Johns, a school complex and community centre where people can come together in an accessible setting, I experienced that however small the island may be, the sense of community is strong. And at the Saba Cares Nursing Home, I had the honour of handing out gifts to all the mothers and grandmothers in the care home on Mother’s Day. 

Naturally we had various government consultations on the programme too. I spoke with Governor Johnson, the island council and the executive council about issues such as Saba’s connectivity, combating crime, climate adaptation and the cost of living.  
 
Many thanks to everyone on Saba who helped make my visit a success. Next stop: St Eustatius!

Today I met with Jonathan Johnson, Saba’s longest-serving Island Governor. It was great to talk with him about his experiences over the past 18 years. 
 
We also discussed Saba’s ties with its neighbouring islands,  particularly in relation to food security, and the progress of the various infrastructure projects on Saba, including Black Rocks Harbor, which is so important for the island’s future economy. 
 
I’m sure that for the people of Saba it must feel unreal that Island Governor Johnson will be stepping down soon. I thanked him very much for his important work for this beautiful island.

El crucero holandés Hondius llegó hoy a salvo a Tenerife. Los pasajeros y la tripulación de la embarcación se someten a controles médicos para continuar su viaje de forma segura. La salud pública es primordial.

Muchas gracias a las autoridades españolas y al primer ministro @sanchezcastejon por hacer esto posible. Muchas gracias por la buena y constructiva cooperación entre los dos países en los últimos días.

I’ve had a great day on St Maarten, making it a successful start to my visit to the Caribbean part of our Kingdom. 
 
Much of the day was devoted to the disastrous impact of hurricanes Irma and Maria, which ravaged the island in 2017, and the reconstruction process since then. I was able to see for myself how much has already been achieved. The progress is truly impressive and speaks volumes about the resilience of the people of St Maarten. 
  
During my visit I spoke with Prime Minister Luc Mercelina, Governor Ajamu Baly, members of the cabinet and members of parliament about various key topics. In addition to the reconstruction operation, we focused on the importance of equal and respectful cooperation within the Kingdom. I also met with the Minister of Justice, Nathalie Tackling, and representatives of the police and the judiciary to discuss another key topic: safety and security on the island. It’s crucial that we keep working together on issues such as border control and organised crime. 
 
I’m very grateful for the warm welcome I received from everyone on St Maarten. Tomorrow I’m off to Saba!

On the first day of my visit to the Caribbean I was welcomed by Prime Minister Luc Mercelina of St Maarten. We discussed the situation on the island and the opportunities and challenges facing St Maarten.  
 
We also spoke about the effect of geopolitical developments on the island, such as the high price of oil. And of course we reflected on the enormous impact that hurricane Irma had on St Maarten in 2017, and the extent to which the island has recovered in the years since. 
 
Another important topic was cooperation within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Prime Minister Mercelina and I agree that we need to work together on the basis of equality and respect, and in the interests of our countries and peoples. I look forward to cooperating closely in the years ahead.

The government attaches great importance to strong, constructive cooperation with the Caribbean part of our Kingdom.

And so I’m glad to be on my way to the country of St Maarten, and the special public bodies of Saba and St Eustatius. From there I will be moving on to the special public body of Bonaire and the countries of Aruba and Curaçao. 

I’m greatly looking forward to my visit.

It was a pleasure to speak for the first time with President @Jaemyung_Lee of the Republic of Korea. Our countries enjoy a long-standing relationship, based on shared interests in the areas of security, industry and renewable energy. 
 
Russia’s war against Ukraine and the situation in the Strait of Hormuz demonstrate just how important international cooperation is to safeguarding a free, safe and secure world. I have offered Dutch assistance where necessary to support the Republic of Korea in its investigation of an attack on one of their cargo ships this week.

As countries with considerable expertise in innovation-driven sectors, such as the battery and semiconductor industries, we have a great deal to learn from each other and can work together effectively. The Netherlands’ expertise in wind energy could play a vital role in helping the Republic of Korea as it works to become more sustainable. I believe we have plenty to build on.

Ethiopia and the Netherlands have a close, long-standing partnership in the areas of trade, sustainable development and migration. In that light it was a pleasure to meet Prime Minister @AbiyAhmedAli today. 

This year our countries mark a century of bilateral trade relations. The Netherlands is Ethiopia’s largest export destination, and also the largest European investor in Ethiopia, with over a hundred Dutch companies operating there, including in the agricultural sector. In the future, we hope to work together even more closely, for instance on climate cooperation. I wished the prime minister every success in organising COP32 in 2027.

We also discussed the global impact of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and the affect this has had on both our countries.

Shocking incident in Washington. Glad that President Trump @Potus and other attendees at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner remained unharmed. 

In a democracy, violence is never the answer; differences of opinion are resolved through dialogue.

The world is in a turbulent state. Wars are being waged close to home and tensions are rising. So it’s important for Europe to come together and shoulder its responsibility. That’s why I’ll be meeting my European counterparts today at the informal EU Council in Cyprus, with a view to working towards solutions to the major issues facing us now.

Yesterday evening we spoke with President Zelenskyy about Ukraine and the support still needed by its people, who live with war on a daily basis. 

We will also be discussing the Middle East and how we can use diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions and take steps towards peace. More practically, we will talk about how to ensure that the people there get the assistance they so badly need. And about how to restore the prospect of a future in which people can rebuild their lives. 

In the meantime the consequences of these conflicts are being felt here in Europe too. The economy in general, businesses and people’s day-to-day lives have all been affected. Europe needs to step up and take measures that offer help now, while also safeguarding our future.That’s why we must make choices about the EU budget, in order to invest in security, cooperation and a sustainable future – the things that really matter.

At times like these it’s all about taking responsibility. For one another. For Europe. And for the future.

The definitive release of the European Union’s €90 billion support package for Ukraine is a very important step. It’s crucial to Ukraine’s fight for its freedom and therefore to our security too. The Netherlands also welcomes the adoption of the 20th sanctions package to keep up the pressure on Russia. 

This afternoon I will be travelling to Cyprus, where this evening and tomorrow I will have further discussions with my European counterparts on support for Ukraine. We will also discuss the situation in the Middle East, the economic impact of high energy prices, and the EU Multiannual Financial Framework.

Had a pleasant first call with Prime Minister @ediramaal of Albania, a key strategic partner in the Western Balkans for both the Netherlands and the EU.

Our economic ties and security cooperation are already strong. We discussed scope for further expanding our partnership, e.g. on infrastructure and tourism. 

Also talked about how Albania is taking significant steps to meet the criteria for the EU accession process. I look forward to meeting PM Rama at the EU-Western Balkans summit in June.

Egypt is an important and strategic partner for the Netherlands in the Middle East, both bilaterally and through the EU. Earlier today 
I spoke on the phone with Egyptian President @AlsisiOfficial about developments in the Middle East, bilateral cooperation, and what we can do to further strengthen that cooperation.
 
I expressed my appreciation for the mediating role being played by Egypt in the region, with regard to both the situation in Gaza and the peace talks between Iran and the US. I thanked the president in particular for Egypt’s significant contribution to the medical evacuations from Gaza. I am pleased that the Netherlands has been able to contribute €2 million to this effort via WHO.
 
We also discussed the violence in Sudan and Egypt’s efforts to bring the warring parties there to a peace agreement, along with what the Netherlands and other European countries can do to contribute to this.
 
The Netherlands is Egypt’s fourth-largest trading partner within the EU. We spoke about opportunities for Dutch businesses in Egypt in areas such as renewable energy, food security, and agriculture and horticulture, with a view to strengthening our cooperation.

🇦🇺🇳🇱 Even though our countries are separated by a vast distance, the bond between the Netherlands and Australia is strong and has deep historical roots. There are, for example, hundreds of thousands of people of Dutch descent living in Australia. I just had a cordial conversation with the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese (@AlboMP).

We discussed the importance of expanding our cooperation in this turbulent world, including in terms of trade between Australia and the EU. We also spoke about the negative consequences of climate change, which are increasingly being felt in Australia and its neighbouring countries.

Naturally, we also discussed the unrest in the Middle East and its impact on the rest of the world, for example in the form of high fuel prices. Finally, I thanked Prime Minister Albanese for Australia’s support for Ukraine in the fight against Russian aggression.

Freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz must not be obstructed in any way. The impact of the current situation is being felt worldwide, including here in the Netherlands. This afternoon, I spoke with the leaders of 50 countries in a video conference to discuss how we can work together to find a solution.

This starts with putting pressure on Iran to respect the principle of free passage. A further possibility is a military mission to secure the Strait of Hormuz once hostilities have ceased. The Netherlands is exploring this, and we are working with allies on the military planning. 

Even following the announced ceasefire, there are still many uncertainties, and developments are unfolding at a rapid pace. That is why we are pursuing various scenarios. One thing is clear: shipping must always be able to pass through the Strait of Hormuz unhindered.

In a highly turbulent world, the role of multilateral organisations such as the United Nations (@UN) is of great value. The UN does important work in the areas of international peace, security and human rights, often under difficult circumstances.

This morning I welcomed Secretary-General @antonioguterres to the Ministry of General Affairs, where he sat in on the weekly cabinet meeting to discuss the UN and developments in the Middle East. We spoke about the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, which is having a major global impact. Further UN priorities include the recovery efforts in Gaza and the situation in the West Bank. To address these issues, it is setting up a new Horizon Fund. I informed the Secretary-General that the Netherlands will contribute €5 million to the fund.

Today, after the Four Freedoms Awards ceremony, I met with President @ZelenskyyUa of Ukraine. Naturally we discussed the current state of the war with Russia – a fight we must not lose sight of, even as unfolding developments in the Middle East demand our attention. Ukraine can count on us. That means we will use sanctions to keep up the pressure on Putin and try to force him to come to the negotiating table.

We will continue pressing for a just and lasting peace for Ukraine, however distant a prospect that may currently seem. After all, it’s clear that in the past few months Putin hasn’t taken a single step in the right direction. So we must also be realistic. And that requires all allies to do what is needed to support Ukraine in this fight.

The Netherlands will continue to support Ukraine. In this regard we are making a firm commitment to collaborating with Ukraine’s defence industry. In part, this means the procurement of drones from Ukrainian companies, but it also entails the co-production of Ukrainian drones by Dutch companies. Today, President @ZelenskyyUa and I gave extra impetus to this deepening of our cooperation by signing a declaration of intent.

Over the coming period we will invest €248 million in drone production in the Netherlands. And I’m glad to note that the first joint project for drone production was launched today, with the signing of a cooperation agreement by the companies VDL and Greentech-Harvest.

We are hereby strengthening the production and innovative capacities of Dutch industry, which is a crucial part of efforts to expand our European defence capabilities.

“On behalf of all the ordinary men, women and children who were thrust overnight into a new reality they did not choose.

On behalf of the children who now go to school in an air-raid shelter.

On behalf of the women who keep their families afloat and their country running by working in factories.

On behalf of the men who’ve had to swap a suit-and-tie for combat fatigues, and are fighting to defend their territory. Metre by metre.

Who are doing so because they know and feel that every square centimetre is a piece not just of Ukraine’s soil, but of its dignity too. That is what they are defending.

President Zelenskyy, Volodymyr: this award is for your country. For you as president. And for all the Ukrainian people.”

Today in Middelburg it was my privilege to join Elizabeth Roosevelt Johnston (the great-granddaughter of President Franklin D. Roosevelt) in presenting the International Four Freedoms Award to President @ZelenskyyUa of Ukraine. 

He accepted the award on behalf of the Ukrainian people as a ‘recognition of the courageous fight for our freedom and democracy under exceptionally difficult circumstances’.

Hablamos sobre la actualidad en Venezuela y la importancia del apoyo internacional permanente a la libertad y la democracia.

🇳🇱🇬🇧 In these times of geopolitical turbulence, it’s reassuring to have a partner and a friend in the United Kingdom, our good North Sea Neighbour. This was reaffirmed today during my visit to Prime Minister @Keir_Starmer in London. 
 
Naturally we discussed the fragile situation in and around Iran. I expressed my appreciation for the UK’s initiative to contribute, with the Netherlands and other allies, to an open Strait of Hormuz. The closure of the Strait is having a big economic impact worldwide. At the same time, we are not losing sight of the war in Ukraine. Ukraine can continue to count on us.
 
Today Prime Minister Starmer and I also took part in a roundtable discussion with energy companies from our two countries, focusing on the current energy crisis that is having a major impact on households and businesses. We must also remain committed to finding long-term solutions, to keep energy affordable and stay on track for a climate-neutral future.

Together with King Willem-Alexander and Queen Máxima (@koninklijkhuis), I visited President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump at the White House this evening.

Our visit focused on the special and deeply rooted bond between the United States and the Netherlands. We talked about our strong trade relations and our security cooperation, including within NATO.

Of course we also discussed the recent developments in and around Iran. It is important that we now work towards a sustainable solution and prevent the situation from escalating further. Russia’s continuing aggression in Ukraine was also a key topic of discussion.

🇳🇱🇺🇸 On Capitol Hill I met with senators from a bipartisan working group on transatlantic relations. In these times of great international tension, a strong US-European relationship is vital, even if we do not agree on everything.
